Issue: 567
Summary: On the latest master branch of OpENer, the report describes a remotely reachable server-side crash triggered by a crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request. The report attributes the underlying corruption to request handling before the visible crash: CreateCommonPacketFormatStructure() accepts a malformed CPF with an invalid item_count/inconsistent length, the unconnected Message Router payload reaches GetAttributeList(), GetAttributeList() parses an attacker-controlled excessively large attribute_count_request and builds an oversized inner Message Router response, and EncodeMessageRouterResponseData() copies that inner response into the outer ENIPMessage without validating remaining destination capacity. According to the report, this overruns message_buffer[512] and overwrites the adjacent current_message_position field; the observed result is that AddIntToMessage() later dereferences the corrupted pointer and crashes. The documented crash is an AddressSanitizer SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136.
Reproduce: 1) Use the latest master branch of OpENer and run a server instance; the report demonstrates the issue on an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer build. 2) Send the provided crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request to the server. The PoC is the hex byte sequence beginning with <6f><00><30><01><30><30><30><30> and continuing exactly as provided in the document. 3) Observe the server abort under AddressSanitizer with a SEGV caused by a READ in AddIntToMessage() at source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c:136:49, with the stack including EncodeSockaddrInfoItemTypeId(), AssembleLinearMessage(), NotifyCommonPacketFormat(), HandleReceivedSendRequestResponseDataCommand(), and HandleReceivedExplictTcpData().
[/SOURCE]

Issue: 557
Summary: OpENer’s explicit messaging path has a remotely reachable out-of-bounds read while decoding CIP padded EPath data. The document states that DecodePaddedEPath decodes attacker-controlled path segments before verifying that the declared path length is fully present in the buffer, and that the decoder does not receive remaining-buffer-length information and performs unchecked reads of *message_runner, message_runner + 1, and 16-bit values. After session registration, crafted SendRRData payloads trigger the fault; under ASan this is reported as a stack-buffer-overflow read in DecodePaddedEPath, and the process aborts, causing denial of service.

Issue: 577
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf is reported vulnerable in the TCP explicit-messaging path (RegisterSession -> SendRRData). A crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request can reach the Connection Manager instance services ForwardClose (0x4E), GetConnectionData (0x56), or SearchConnectionData (0x57) and trigger a stack-buffer-overflow read. The report attributes this to missing minimum request-body length validation in these handlers after Message Router path decoding: a long but syntactically acceptable padded EPath can consume the remaining CIP payload, leave request_data_size == 0, and the handlers still call GetUintFromMessage() / GetUdintFromMessage() on message_router_request->data. The reported result is an out-of-bounds read past the stack receive buffer, with stated impact of at least remote unauthenticated denial of service.

Issue: 576
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf has a remotely reachable server-side memory corruption issue in the unconnected explicit-message SendRRData path. In GetAttributeList(), the response-space estimation for each returned attribute entry is 4 bytes too small because it counts the attribute value length but omits the fixed per-entry metadata that is later written: Attribute ID (2 bytes), status (1 byte), and reserved (1 byte). A valid GetAttributeList request against Identity instance 1 that repeatedly requests attribute 1 corrupts outer response metadata during response assembly; when the request also includes valid optional sockaddr info items 0x8000 and 0x8001, AssembleLinearMessage() continues encoding those CPF items and eventually crashes in AddIntToMessage() with a corrupted current_message_position.
